subject: Re: Eval continuity — structure of bridging offer and operational asks
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@orionai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orion AI Legal <contracts@orionai.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC continuity + short bridge — ask

Jordan —

Thanks again for the pilot this month. Our product team would like to extend the evaluation for two reasons: 1) a late internal spike in usage consumed more credits than expected; and 2) a small integration gap on our end that needs a repeat run with full data. We don't want to stop the work but we also can't commit to a full annual license yet.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a one-month continuity/bridge that:
- preserves the existing environment and model pinning,
- adds 100k additional tokens of compute credit (non-refundable) for the month, and
- grants a 10% discount on the per-token rate for any top-up beyond the 100k?

We'll need an approved SOW and a short contract addendum from your side (legal will review). Can you share what structure you'd recommend? Also thinking about an SLA for availability during the bridge (our devs will be running daily batch jobs).

Appreciate quick guidance — we want to avoid losing momentum.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Director of AI Engineering
Orion AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@orionai.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC continuity + short bridge — ask

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear ask and context. We can absolutely support a short continuity plan without pushing straight to an annual commitment. Proposal (high level):

1) Continuity window: 30 days from activation; we keep the same model pin and environment config.
2) Credit pool: 100k tokens included upfront (applies to both streaming and batched jobs).
3) Top-up pricing: a reduced token rate for any additional consumption during the 30 days — proposing 12% off list (slightly more conservative than your 10% request so we can keep runway for other pilots).
4) Operational SLA: 99.5% availability for the continuity pool; included priority support (one dedicated SE hour/week) and an on-call escalation path for urgent batch runs.

I'll attach a short SOW and a one-page addendum that covers the top-up pricing and the rollback plan if Orion opts not to convert. Two asks on our side:
- Can you confirm the expected weekly ingestion pattern so we can size burst capacity (e.g., 1 big nightly batch vs. continuous small requests)?
- Legal: if Orion's counsel needs changes to the addendum, please flag the redlines you consider critical so we can triage.

If that all sounds OK, I'll loop in Priyom to size the bridge technically and Laura to confirm contract language.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC continuity + short bridge — ask

Team — forwarding a request from Orion (Alyssa) that wants a 30-day bridge with a 100k token top-up and a small discount on incremental usage. My recommended commercial: include 100k tokens + 12% off token rate for the month, 99.5% SLA and 1 SE hour/week. Attachments: draft SOW and offer (see folder).

Priyom — can you confirm feasibility for nightly batch jobs of ~40k tokens/day for two weeks (peak) and steady ~8k/day otherwise? If that spikes above burst threshold, we'll need to propose burst capacity pricing.

Laura — are there any non-starters in a short one-page addendum that just covers term (30d), credits, top-up rate, and a rollback clause? We want to keep legal review minimal.

Quick replies good — this is time-sensitive for their dev sprint.

—Jordan
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC continuity + short bridge — ask

Jordan —

Feasible. Nightly batches at 40k/day for ~10–14 days are okay if we provision a small burst queue; that will fit within a 100k pool if they smooth after the peak. Two notes:
- If they hit sustained >80k/day for more than 3 consecutive days, we should automatically throttle and surface an alert to them (we'll include that in the SOW).
- For the 12% discounted top-up, recommend we cap the volume eligible for the discount at 500k tokens to limit exposure.

I'll mark the SE hours and standby windows in the SOW draft.

—Priyom
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@orionai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orion AI Legal <contracts@orionai.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC continuity + short bridge — ask

Jordan —

Thanks, that structure is very close to what we need. A couple of quick counterpoints from our side:
- The team prefers a 10% off rate rather than 12% — can you do 10% if we commit to a conversion conversation during the month? We'd be open to a short internal checkpoint and a conversion decision by day 20.
- Can you remove the 500k cap on discounted top-ups? We don't expect to use that much but it helps us budget predictability.
- On SLA: 99.5% is acceptable but we'd like a small service credit (1% monthly credit on fees for continuity window) if availability drops below the target.

Legal (contracts@orionai.com) — we'll review the addendum and SOW; expect redlines around indemnity and data handling.

If you can accept the 10% and remove the cap, we can sign quickly and start the bridge on Monday.

—Alyssa
